revision_rule.note: The same permission is established by the assertion-specific sampling text and checker always examples in this clause.
The 2012 rule prohibits output and non-const ref arguments but does not prohibit inout arguments; its state-preservation and side-effect restrictions otherwise match.
The 2017 rule prohibits output and non-const ref arguments but does not prohibit inout arguments; 2023 adds the inout prohibition.
The 2012 rule permits $ as an actual to an untyped formal with restricted uses, but does not include the 2023 permission for $ as a default actual to a nested checker.
The 2017 rule permits $ as a checker input actual under the untyped/use restrictions, but does not permit it as a declared default actual or forwarding it as a nested checker's default argument.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no checker rewriting algorithm or flattened-checker legality guarantee.
